input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: § 2.1 imposes a multi-year (three-year) USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay minimum on Customer with expressly no reduction or termination rights — the playbook walk-away position. It also directly contradicts § 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment, and § 7.1, which ties Fees to Order Forms and bars minimum-use charges. Redline replaces § 2.1 with a no-minimum/usage-or-ordered-services formulation (preferred position); a 12-month, reducible commitment with a true-up is offered as fallback in the comment.

proposal.summary: Remove the three-year USD 2M take-or-pay commitment and confirm fees are payable only for Services ordered or used.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a multi-year take-or-pay minimum with no reduction or termination right, and § 2.1 also contradicts Vendor's acknowledgement in § 12.3 that we have made no minimum-volume commitment. We have replaced it so that fees are payable only for Services ordered or used under § 7.1; if a commitment is commercially essential, we could consider one limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.

ops.oldText: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
ops.newText: 2.1 Customer has no minimum purchase, volume, or take-or-pay commitment. Fees are payable only for Services that Customer orders under an Order Form or actually uses, in accordance with Section 7.1.
